thread.title: Groups That Are Leading Nasdaq Higher - Cramer's Mad Money (6/4/18)

author: SA Editor Mohit Manghnani
title: Groups That Are Leading Nasdaq Higher - Cramer's Mad Money (6/4/18)
text:
Stocks discussed on the in-depth session of Jim Cramer's Mad Money TV Program, Monday , June 4.
The Nasdaq showed positive strength on Monday. It was not just the FANG stocks that led the charge, the market found leaders in other groups and it turned out to be a great day for bulls. Apart from FANG stocks, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) led the charge as the WWDC kicked off and it hit a 52-week high. It has a good business model that can't be beaten.
The semiconductor group also showed strength with Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA ) reaching an all-time high. The group was under pressure after the Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM ) merger with Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO ) was blocked. "It took a little bit, but ultimately, the market was able to draw a distinction between chip companies that are pure cellphone plays and the ones that aren't," said Cramer.
The cloud kings and some biotech stocks helped push Nasdaq up as well. On the takeover side, Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ) acquired developer platform Github for $7.5B and it closed up 0.9%. Starbucks (NASDAQ: SBUX ) was the only disappointment as chairman Howard Schultz stepped down.
Only a week ago the market was fretting about Italian bond yields and how it would affect global markets. Cramer called it a non-event that was made loud by terrified investors. A week later, the yields are back where they started. "Now, obviously the press can't avoid a story like this, but you can give people some context, and when it comes to Italy, a little context could've gone a long way," said Cramer.
"That is the way this business works: bulls are always punished more harshly for being wrong than the bears are. Here's the bottom line: the Nasdaq was left for dead not that long ago, but turns out it was just resting," concluded Cramer.
Off the charts As consumer sentiment and job growth rises, restaurant stocks will rise too. Cramer went to the charts with the help of technician Bob Lang to review the stocks in the casual dining space.
The stock of Chipotle (NYSE: CMG ) was crushed in 2015 from an e-coli breakout and it has been limping since. It managed to find a bottom at $240 and has started to grow after a good last quarter and analyst faith . The stock's RSI is highly positive after their earnings and the volume trends are favorable as well. Despite the growth, the stock is not in overbought territory. The stock has more room to run and Lang thinks it can touch $480-500 in the near future.
Del Taco (NASDAQ: TACO ) is smaller compared to Chipotle, but the stock is up 25% from its lows in March. The MACD indicator has made a bullish crossover and the RSI is positive. "While the stock is approaching the ceiling of resistance from where it gapped down in March at $12.50, right near the 200-day moving average, Lang believes it can make a run at that level and then push higher," said Cramer.
The small-cap Mexican chain El Pollo Loco (NASDAQ: LOCO ) rallied till its 50-week moving average met the ceiling of resistance. "El Pollo Loco recently made a higher low; that's a good sign, and the volume trends have been improving, meaning the volume is higher on up days than down days. Meanwhile, the Relative Strength Index keeps climbing, and in April, the MACD made that bullish crossover," added Cramer.
"The charts, as interpreted by Bob Lang, suggest that Chipotle, Del Taco and El Pollo Loco still have plenty of upside here and I think he's got a strong case. That said, Chipotle is the only one of these three that's not extremely speculative, so please be extra careful with the other two," he concluded.
CEO interview - Wyndham Hotels & Resorts (NYSE: WH ) Wyndham Hotels and Resorts is a spinoff from Wyndham Destinations (NYSE: WYND ) which was formerly known as Wyndham Worldwide and it debuted on NYSE . Cramer interviewed CEO Geoff Ballotti to hear about the roadmap of the newly independent company.
Ballotti said being an independent company, the shareholders can expect consistent income in the form of dividends and share-buybacks. They can also have a strategy around deploying their cash towards M&A.
Commenting on threats from sharing economy players like Airbnb ( AIRB ), he said, "There's always too much made of the Airbnb threat especially in the economy, in the mid-scale segments, in the non-urban suburban roadside environments in which we play. We believe that for far too long, millennials have wanted an upscale experience at an economy price and that's what we're doing with all of our brands. And to see our brands so nationally ranked and the health that they are enjoying today – take Days Inn, which years ago was ranked tenth. It's now third place on the J.D. Power rankings and we want to see continue to move up."
The company has 20 different brands across the globe and their franchisees see opportunities to grow.
CEO interview - Henry Schein (NASDAQ: HSIC ) Cramer interviewed CEO Stanley Bergman of Henry Schein, a company which has been under pressure on growth concerns. Bergman said that the company had a good last quarter and they reiterated the guidance of 12-15% EPS growth.
Many believe that online dental supplies are taking market share from them but their research shows otherwise. They have recently partnered with WebMD and it will help streamline the dentistry practices his company serves. "On the dental side, they have software that also generates demand for visits to the dentist. With our practice management systems, and we have the leading practice management systems throughout the world. You put the two together and we believe we can help dentists operate a more efficient practice so that they could provide better clinical care," said Bergman.
He was excited about the upcoming spinoff of the animal care business as vets write more prescriptions for animals.
Viewer calls taken by Cramer MercadoLibre (NASDAQ: MELI ): It's a tough stock to own. Don't buy.
Stamps.com (NASDAQ: STMP ): It is the winner in its category but it's a pricey stock.
Bojangles (NASDAQ: BOJA ): It's a good stock that is not expensive and has upside.
Hain Celestial (NASDAQ: HAIN ): It's a company with struggling fundamentals and it's expensive.
